sources.entry: Unison - Unison is a file-synchronization tool for OSX, Unix, and Windows. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 deb/OCaml

summary.one_liner: Unison is a bidirectional file-synchronization tool that keeps two replicas of a file tree on different hosts or disks in step across POSIX systems and Windows.
summary.what_it_does: Unison synchronizes two replicas of a directory tree that may live on different hosts or disks, with each side modified independently. Non-conflicting changes propagate automatically in both directions, while conflicting updates are detected and shown to the user. It runs as a user-level program using normal system calls, so it needs no kernel changes, no superuser rights on either host, and no FUSE. Remote sync typically goes over ssh, or directly over TCP, and it uses an rsync-like compression protocol to transfer small changes to large files efficiently. A "repeat" mode can use a filesystem monitor to sync soon after changes happen. The README says synchronized data stays readable and writable while offline, since Unison copies the data rather than mounting a network filesystem.
use_cases: two-way sync between a laptop and a server
keep home and work folders in step
sync files across Windows and Unix machines
continuous sync with a filesystem monitor
how_to_run: Get Unison from a packaging system (many GNU/Linux distributions provide binary packages) or build from source
Follow the building instructions in the project wiki or the CI recipes referenced in the README
Use the most recent formal release or a newer git master build; older releases are not maintained
notable: Bidirectional sync that detects and displays conflicting updates instead of silently overwriting them
User-level program requiring no kernel changes, root access, or FUSE
rsync-like compression for transferring small changes to large files
Optional repeat mode with a filesystem monitor for near-immediate sync
Over 25 years in use according to the README
caveats: Only a very small team maintains it (the README estimates 2.5 people and 0.1 FTE), and it asks users not to seek help in the issue tracker
Earlier versions are unsupported; bug reports are not accepted for them, even though distributions often ship 2.51 or 2.48
